Fleetline redesign — pick a number

Three materially distinct design directions for the Alexa+ fleet-command simulator, each rendered live from the real product (1440×900, real autodemo mission, real MCP traffic). Same machine, same data, three design languages.

Reply with 1, 2, or 3 — or open any of them live and drive it yourself before deciding:
1 · Signal — http://127.0.0.1:3000/?theme=signal (current default)
2 · Ops — http://127.0.0.1:3000/?theme=ops
3 · Press — http://127.0.0.1:3000/?theme=press
Add &autodemo=1 to any URL to watch a mission run hands-free. Nothing is merged until you pick.

1 · Signal Recommended

Dark product-glass — the "serious 2026 dev-tool" register (Linear/Vercel class). Deep charcoal, layered low-alpha surfaces, indigo/cyan signals, serif-free system type. Conversation left, instrument dashboard right, stat strip on top. ?theme=signal — current default.

Computed evidence: WCAG contrast failures 0 · glyph overlaps 0 · horizontal overflow 0 · min font 10px (audited in live DOM, 103 text nodes). Role-grouped roster (fetchers ×4 / analysts ×3 / composer ×1), progress bars, MCP tool-call chips, phase-coded event feed.

2 · Ops

Amber operations console — mission-control register. Flat near-black with a hairline instrument grid, amber phosphor accents, LED stat cells, monospace-first type, console-transcript chat (no bubbles), segmented progress bars. Distinctly "fleet ops". ?theme=ops

Computed evidence: WCAG contrast failures 0 · glyph overlaps 0 · horizontal overflow 0 · min font 10px. Highest data density of the three; the most "operator" personality.

3 · Press

Light editorial broadsheet — print register. Warm paper, near-black ink, kyanite-blue accent, serif display numerals, hairline rules instead of cards, transcript with quote bars, dotted wire-feed. The only light theme; pops against dark editors and reads crisply on camera. ?theme=press

Computed evidence: WCAG contrast failures 0 · glyph overlaps 0 · horizontal overflow 0 · min font 10px. Boldest departure from typical hacker dashboards.

For reference: the "before" (what earned "ugly as fuck")

Design PM recommendation: 1 · Signal — it most directly answers "serious 2026 dev-tool product" on camera while staying legible at 1440×900; 2 · Ops is the strongest personality play (judges remember mission-control vibes, and it matches Fleetline's voice-command story); 3 · Press is the taste wildcard — cleanest reading on camera, but furthest from the dev-tool category judges expect. All three pass the same computed legibility gates; the choice is brand posture, not quality. Stills embedded from real headless-Chrome renders of the live server, identical demo state per capture. Receipt: docs/DESIGN-2026-09-25.md. Times PT.
